captions.t: If your request could mean two different things,
Cohort Studio asks first.
Every answer shows how many samples it would keep,
so you choose with the numbers in front of you.
Every step shows exactly how many samples are left.
When a join starts counting the same sample twice,
it's flagged in pink.
One click on Fix it,
and every sample counts once again.
Each cohort gets an honest verdict: ready, conditional, or blocked.
Open it to see every check behind it,
and what a person still needs to review.
When it's ready,
download the sample list,
and a Python script that rebuilds the cohort exactly.
Or open it on the canvas,
and keep shaping it visually.
This is your cohort as a pipeline.
Every card is one step,
with the real count from the engine.
And every wire is drawn to scale,
so you can see where samples drop away.
A join that adds extra rows turns pink.
Tap See why to X-ray a real patient,
and watch their slides become rows.
Then one click on Fix,
and every sample counts once.
Press Add to open the blocks.
Drag one onto any wire,
and it slots right in.
If it needs data from another table,
the join is added for you.
Switch on grain lanes to see what one row stands for:
a patient, a sample,
or several rows per sample.
A join that double counts drops a lane,
and its fix brings it back.
Open Code to see the same cohort as SQL, Python,
or the raw steps.
The SQL isn't just written.
It's run,
and checked against the engine,
step by step.
Pick any two cohorts: saved ones, favourites,
or two versions of the same cohort.
Both are rerun on the same frozen data,
so the comparison is fair.
See exactly who the two cohorts share,
drawn to scale,
with plain sentences that say what the numbers mean.
Then see how they differ:
who is in each,
which data they have,
and survival curves,
with one record per patient.
